claims.text: As-processed HfNbTiVAl10 has a well-characterized hierarchical heterostructure at room temperature.
In situ high-speed X-ray tomography can capture the internal microstructural evolution of HfNbTiVAl10 during microtensile and microfracture loading.
Phase connectivity, void distributions, local crack-tip environments, and phase bridging can be quantitatively extracted as three-dimensional descriptors from the tomography images.
Machine learning can use structural or compositional descriptors to predict mechanical properties of aluminum-containing refractory high-entropy alloys.
An AI algorithm trained on tomography descriptors and independent mechanical data can map the descriptors directly to macroscopic mechanical responses of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed tool can predict Young's modulus for HfNbTiVAl10 within 10% of independent measurements.
The proposed tool can predict yield strength for HfNbTiVAl10 within 10% of independent measurements.
The proposed tool can predict fracture behavior for HfNbTiVAl10 within 10% of independent measurements.
The proposed predictions can be produced in minutes.
The proposed method will improve efficiency by approximately 15–20% relative to conventional simulation methods.
Direct AI mapping from microstructural descriptors to mechanical responses can bypass lengthy finite-element simulations.
Traditional finite-element simulations require extensive computational resources and time.
Traditional finite-element simulations often have prediction uncertainties exceeding 10%.
Young's modulus and yield strength can be calculated from stress–strain curves obtained in microscale mechanical tests.
Observed microscale deformation and fracture evolution can be correlated with features in the corresponding load or stress–strain response.
Failure to resolve critical subsurface heterogeneities can prevent reliable prediction of mechanical behavior.
Excessive imaging noise, insufficiently general descriptors, or limited training data can prevent the AI algorithm from reliably correlating tomography descriptors with mechanical responses.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis broadly promises predictions within 10% error, but the falsification rule permits up to 70% of specimens to exceed 10% error without decisive falsification. This success criterion is substantially weaker than the stated prediction claim.
